display.title: Asarah B'Teves: A Time to Be Sad and a Time to Remember
display.summary_short: On the tenth of Teves, Uncle Yossi explains why there is a time to be sad, and tells how Nevuchadnetzar's siege of Yerushalayim began the road to the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash.
display.summary_long: A talk for Asarah B'Teves from the Tzivos Hashem radio show, given on the day itself. Uncle Yossi reviews the Hebrew months, Tishrei, Cheshvan, Kislev and now Teves, the fourth month, and reveals that today is the tenth of Teves, a sad day in Jewish history. Shlomo HaMelech taught that there is a time for everything: a time to be happy and also a time to be sad, not to stay sad, but to learn from the mistakes of the past and serve Hashem with a pure heart. On the tenth of Teves the armies of Nevuchadnetzar, king of Bavel, surrounded Yerushalayim and sealed its gates, and the people inside grew weak from hunger and thirst. The siege led to the breach of the walls on the seventeenth of Tammuz and, three weeks later, to the destruction of the Beis HaMikdash on Tisha B'Av. The answer to such troubles is to keep learning Torah and doing mitzvos, for, as Dovid HaMelech wrote, the Guardian of Israel neither slumbers nor sleeps.
display.lesson: We remember sad days to learn from the past; as long as we learn Torah and keep the mitzvos, Hashem guards and protects us.

date.note: 'Today is the tenth of Teves'; filename episode 507 aired Tuesday 10 Teves 5752. The same talk also aired in other years.
